reason: A lax network of veinlets is a normal description of venation.
Lax cymes are normal.
Hypocotyl length is a normal measurement.
Wrinkled or rugose pods are normal.
Obovate pods are normal.
Surface texture of drupes (smooth, striate, dull) fits the attribute.
Sessile or stipitate follicles are a normal attachment description.
A subcylindrical floral disc is correct. The examples are about the disc.
Striate primary veins (prominent and striate below) are a valid surface description.
A woody pyrene or stone wall is normal. One example is about a whole fruit wall.
Slender fruit pedicels are normal.
'Orné de' here means a lip bearing rows of glands or hairs. That is indumentum or glands, not an ornamentation quality. A rule would map 'orné de X' to has-part X and not to ornamented.
Apiculate describes an apex (leaf, fruit or bract tip). A placenta is not apiculate, so the examples were probably attached to the wrong part.
A spreading floral disc is valid. 'Divergents' may refer to other parts.
The twisting in the examples ('tordu vers le sommet', 'in the middle') belongs to organs such as fruit, style or awn, not to a short shoot. The part is wrong.
A cup-shaped epichile is a standard orchid description.
'Subentier' describes a margin (almost entire). PATO 'unstructured' is the wrong reading, and the bearer should be the margin.
Convex bracts are normal.
'Pseudopétiole ailé' describes a winged petiole or pseudopetiole, not the lamina base. A rule would need to tell a decurrent lamina base from a winged petiole.
The examples measure internodes (the stem between nodes), not the node. The part is wrong, and the bearer should be the internode.
The number of catkins per cluster is an amount of catkins. This fits the counted-part rule.
Keeled glumes are standard in grasses. 'Without keels' is negated and needs care.
Impressed or immersed ovules are a valid placentation description.
Corolla lobe width is normal. The 'wide' form is a plain measurement.

Bract length is normal. The examples also include squamellae, comparisons with sepals and internodes, and a mix of parts. A rule would send comparisons ('exceeding', 'times as long as') to a separate pattern.
Cicatrose (scarred) twigs and stems are normal.
A hollowed (concave) orchid column apex is a valid description.
A woolly (lanate) perianth is valid.
The scars are on the brachyblast (a short shoot) and not on the inflorescence. The part is wrong.
Narrowing 'at mouth' describes pitchers or tubular organs, not the leaf as a whole. A rule would need the organ to be named (pitcher, tube).
'Nectar glands dense' describes the density of glands on the nectary. That fits a has-part gland count better than a nectary quality. A rule would send it to the gland part.
'Hardened inside' describes a fruit wall or endocarp, not a corolla lobe. The part is wrong.
A fleshy rachis is normal.
A horny (hard) margin on a spine shield is valid. The hardness belongs to the shield margin.
Spathe limb length is normal. 'Much longer' and 'blade longer' are comparisons.
A tessellated stem surface (leaf scars and tubercles) is valid.
A pendent rostellum is a standard orchid description.
Small root nodules are valid.
'Squamellae' in sedges are perianth scales or bristles, not grass lodicules. A rule would need the family (Cyperaceae vs Poaceae) to pick the right part.
A cleft perigynium (dorsally cleft beak) is valid in Carex.
A dimidiate involucel is asymmetrical, so the reading is correct.
An opaque leaf sheath is valid. The count is low.
The thickness is probably that of the axis or of the whole inflorescence and not of the staminate zone. A rule would need to know what is measured.
A rugose or rugulose thallus surface is valid.
A serrate leaf tip is valid. The margin near the tip carries the serration.
Fruit odour is a valid attribute.
Shallow fissures or furrows in bark are valid. 'Stripes' is a doubtful example.
Rosette width is valid. The dimensions are given as length × width.
'Antrorse' usually describes teeth, spines or hairs on a lobe, not the lobe itself. A rule would need the bearer to be the teeth or hairs.
'Basal sinuses closed' describes the sinus (the gap between lobes). The lamina itself is not closed, so the bearer is wrong.
The examples are about an apex or about scale leaves, not the whole leaf. Colourless leaves occur in achlorophyllous plants. A rule would need whole-leaf scope.
Colourless rhizoids are valid.
'Cells obscure' describes the cells of the tunic, which are a different part from the tunic. The pair arises from a wrong reading.
Recurved stigma lobes are valid.
The shape of a pseudostaminode is valid. Some examples are about other parts (the apex), so the shape rule needs care.
The triangular shape belongs to the teeth on the margin, not to the margin. The bearer is wrong, and it should be the leaf tooth.
The inconspicuous item is a part (indumentum, flowers) and not the whole plant. The bearer is wrong.
A papillate cypsela surface is a texture. The reading is correct.
Nectary size is valid. 'Reduced to a gland patch' is a further reading of size.
A dark midvein is a colour description, so 'low brightness' fits.
